description: Do not extend ':ignoreModulesAndTests', even via 'config:recommended' or
'config:best-practices': it ignores '**/test/**', and the chainsaw fixtures under ci/test/
pin the same images the modules run, so their pins would drift unreported. The
'kubernetes.ignorePaths' entry below is unrelated (see disable-updates.json).
internalChecksFilter 'strict': an update whose minimumReleaseAge has not elapsed gets no
branch and no PR -- a soak is a silent hold, not a delay; override-release-age.json depends
on this.
The flux and kubernetes managerFilePatterns include ci/ and components/: fixtures and
shared components carry pins of their own.
rebaseWhen 'conflicted', NOT 'behind-base-branch': main's branch protection has
required_status_checks.strict = false, so being behind base does not block a merge and
rebasing for freshness alone costs a full CI re-run. Measured from a real scheduled run
(2026-08-22T00:21Z): 'Branch is behind base branch and needs rebasing' fired for 12 of 12
open branches, every one was force-pushed, and seconds later the same run read the status it
had just invalidated -- 'Branch status yellow' on all six PRs it then considered for
automerge, so none merged. With ~12 merges/day into main and a 6-hourly schedule, main moves
again before the next evaluation and the cycle repeats: Renovate never sees one of its own
branches green. The trade this makes is explicit: a bot PR now merges having been tested
against the main it branched from rather than the current tip. That is the same staleness
strict = false already accepts for human PRs, and scheduled-baseline.yaml re-runs the suites
against main. Restore 'behind-base-branch' if strict is ever turned back on.
